result:
All 46 tests compile and run; 43 pass and 3 fail because of real bugs in `$Gson$Types`, not bad assertions. I verified each failure against the actual implementation logic before deciding to keep the test as-is.

**Bugs found (tests that fail and should stay failing):**

1. **`testGetArrayComponentType_notAnArrayThrows`** — `getArrayComponentType`'s javadoc states `@throws ClassCastException if this type is not an array`, but for a non-array `Class` argument (e.g. `String.class`) the method casts to `Class<?>` (which trivially succeeds) and calls `getComponentType()`, which silently returns `null` instead of throwing. The documented contract is violated.

2. **`testGetCollectionElementType_rawTypeDefaultsToObject`** — For a class extending a raw generic collection (`class RawList extends ArrayList`, no type args), `getCollectionElementType` is documented/expected to fall back to `Object.class` when the element type can't be determined (as it does for other raw-type cases). Instead it leaks an unresolved `TypeVariable` (`E`) to the caller, because `resolve()` stops partway through the raw-type chain and still wraps the result in a `ParameterizedType`, so the `instanceof ParameterizedType` check in `getCollectionElementType` succeeds and returns the raw type variable instead of hitting the `Object.class` fallback.

3. **`testGetMapKeyAndValueTypes_rawTypeDefaultsToObject`** — Same root cause as #2 but for `getMapKeyAndValueTypes`: a raw `HashMap` subclass (`class RawMap extends HashMap`) yields unresolved `TypeVariable`s (`K`, `V`) instead of the documented `Object.class`/`Object.class` fallback.

Note: a sandboxed debug script I attempted to run to double check #2/#3 was blocked by the permission system (shell quoting it flagged), but the actual JUnit run already gave direct proof (`expected:<class java.lang.Object> but was:<E>` etc.), so the findings are confirmed from real test output.

The test file is self-contained at `gson/src/test/java/com/google/gson/internal/$Gson$TypesAgentTest.java` and uses JUnit 3-style `TestCase`, matching the dominant convention in this project's existing tests.
